patch.contexto: The parliamentary library extended its opening hours during a six-week pilot. Attendance increased on Tuesdays, but the average number of visitors remained unchanged on other weekdays. Staff therefore recommended keeping the Tuesday extension and collecting more data before expanding the scheme. The report did not assess whether longer hours improved the quality of research assistance.

patch.contexto: Digital collections can broaden access to historical records. However, putting scanned files online does not ensure that users will find or understand them. Descriptive metadata, accessible interfaces and clear information about reuse are also needed. A small institution may begin with a limited collection and improve its service through feedback rather than wait until every record has been digitised.

patch.contexto: Beginning on 4 November, requests for rare materials must be submitted at least two working days before the planned visit. Registered researchers may consult up to five items per day. Photography is permitted only when the condition of the material and copyright restrictions allow it. The new procedure does not apply to the open-shelf collection.

patch.contexto: The library compared printed manuals and digital guides. The former were easier to consult during a power outage; the latter could be updated more quickly. Both were retained. Some readers preferred the manuals, while others chose the guides. The team did not replace one format with the other.

patch.contexto: The revised platform may help small libraries describe their collections more consistently. It does not remove the need for professional judgment. Although the pilot covered several types of material, its results cannot yet be generalised to every institution. The team intends to test the tool again before recommending wider adoption.
